Metadata.InquiriesOrToReportAnIssue: For questions or comments, contact info@skinvision.com. For refunds, contact support@skinvision.com within 30 days of purchase for 3-month or yearly plans [SOURCE 2, 5].
Metadata.RegulatoryApprovalStatusIfApplicable: The SkinVision app is a regulated medical device with a European CE marking, TGA approval, and ISO certification [SOURCE 3, 5].
Metadata.GlobalAvailability: SkinVision has partnerships with health insurers, cancer clinics, and research universities in the United Kingdom, Australia, Germany, the Netherlands, and New Zealand [SOURCE 5].
Metadata.Summary: SkinVision is a dermatologist-approved service that helps users assess skin spots and moles for common types of skin cancer, including melanoma. Users take a photo with their smartphone and receive a risk indication within 30 seconds, with recommendations on the next steps [SOURCE 5].
Metadata.Keywords: skin cancer detection; melanoma; mole check; skin spot assessment; dermatology; AI; risk assessment

UsesAndDirections.IntendedUseAndWorkflow: SkinVision is intended to empower users to self-examine their skin, increase their knowledge of when to act, and provide accurate skin cancer detection and personalized skin health advice. Users can check their skin with the Smart Check Camera, create a Body Map to track spots, and identify their Skin Type and Risk Profile [SOURCE 3].
UsesAndDirections.PrimaryIntendedUsers: Individuals concerned about skin cancer, doctors, pharmaceutical companies, and health insurers [SOURCE 1, 3].
UsesAndDirections.NecessaryKnowledgeExpertise: Users need a smartphone to take photos of skin spots. The SkinVision service is not intended to replace traditional methods or be a substitute for visits to a healthcare professional [SOURCE 3, 5].
UsesAndDirections.HowToUse: Download the SkinVision app, take a photo of a skin spot or mole, and receive a risk indication within 60 seconds. Users can also store photos to monitor changes over time and share them with their doctor [SOURCE 3, 5].
UsesAndDirections.TargetedPatientPopulation: Individuals concerned about detecting skin cancer early [SOURCE 3, 5]. The service is not intended for use on persons under the age of 18 [SOURCE 5].

Warnings.DeveloperSuppliedWarnings: The SkinVision Service is not intended to replace traditional methods for the evaluation of skin cancer risk level, does not give a diagnosis, and is not a substitute for visits to a healthcare professional. The SkinVision Service is not intended for use on persons under the age of 18 years old [SOURCE 5].

TrustIngredients.AISystemFacts: The SkinVision app merges AI technology with the expertise of skin health professionals and dermatologists. The SkinVision Service algorithm has a sensitivity of greater than 90% in the detection of the three most common types of skin cancer (Malignant Melanoma (MM), Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) and Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC)) and a specificity of 89% on SkinVision’s user population.
TrustIngredients.ModelType: AI-based algorithm for skin cancer detection
TrustIngredients.InteractionWithOtherSystems: SkinVision connects customers, doctors, and insurers to optimize skin health. It also integrates with health insurance providers.
TrustIngredients.OutcomesAndOutput: The app provides a risk indication of skin spots and moles for the most common types of skin cancer within 60 seconds and recommendations on the next steps to take, including whether to visit a healthcare professional.
TrustIngredients.TypeAndValueOfSolutionOutput: Risk assessment of skin spots and moles, indicating the likelihood of skin cancer.
TrustIngredients.ExplanationForHowAnOutputIsGenerated: SkinVision uses an algorithm to assess moles or skin spots for cancerous signs based on photos taken with a smartphone. This service is quality assured by a team of dermatology experts.
TrustIngredients.InputDataSource: Images of skin spots and moles taken with a smartphone camera.
TrustIngredients.OutputInputDataType: Input: Images of skin spots/moles. Output: Risk assessment (risk indication)

UsefulnessEfficacy.GoalOfMetrics: The goal is to provide accurate and timely skin cancer detection and personalized skin health advice [SOURCE 3]. SkinVision aims to detect skin cancer at an early stage when it’s more likely to be treatable [SOURCE 5].
UsefulnessEfficacy.Result: The SkinVision Service algorithm has a sensitivity of greater than 90% in the detection of the three most common types of skin cancer (Malignant Melanoma (MM), Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) and Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC)) and a specificity of 89% on SkinVision’s user population [SOURCE 3].
UsefulnessEfficacy.Interpretation: Early detection is key to prevention and timely treatment. Over 95% of skin cancers can be successfully treated if they are found early [SOURCE 5]. SkinVision can help detect skin cancer at an early stage when it’s more likely to be treatable [SOURCE 5].
UsefulnessEfficacy.TestType: The SkinVision app uses an algorithm to assess moles or skin spots for cancerous signs [SOURCE 5]. Clinically validated AI-based algorithm [SOURCE 3].
UsefulnessEfficacy.TestingDataDescription: SkinVision users have received more than 3.5 million risk assessments and the app has found over 50,000 cases of melanoma and other types of skin cancer [SOURCE 5].
UsefulnessEfficacy.ValidationProcessAndJustification: SkinVision is a clinically validated, regulated medical device. It has a CE mark, TGA approval, and ISO certification [SOURCE 3]. The app is quality assured by a team of dermatology experts [SOURCE 5].
